newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Japanese emperor revisits Brasilia, 30 years on.
newsitem.headline: Japanese emperor revisits Brasilia, 30 years on.

text.p: Japanese Emperor Akihito toured the futuristic centre of the Brazilian capital on Tuesday and addressed Congress on the third full day of a two-week trip to Brazil and Argentina.

Akihito, the first Japanese emperor to visit South America, said he recalled a visit he made to Brasilia in 1967 while crown prince and how the city, then only seven years old, was only half built in the midst of an arid wilderness.

He recalled how impressed he had been by the monumental design of the purpose-built capital and the architectural symbolism of the central Three Powers Square which houses the presidential palace, Congress and Brazil's supreme court.
"I suppose that 30 years on, some of the congressmen I met then are present today," the emperor, accompanied by Empress Michiko, told a joint session of Congress' two houses.
Akihito also paid tribute to the roughly 1.3 million Brazilians of Japanese descent, the largest overseas Japanese community.

"I am very pleased by the fact that Brazilians who share the blood of the Japanese are contributing in various sectors of society, including the national Congress, towards Brazil's progress," he said, speaking in Japanese.
The couple are also meeting members of the Japanese community in Brasilia, inaugurating a Japanese garden and dining with President Fernando Henrique Cardoso.
Later in the week they travel to Belo Horizonte, Sao Paulo, Curitiba and Rio de Janeiro before flying to Buenos Aires on June 9 for a three-day visit to Argentina.
